scope: Source preparation and proposed teaching sequence, not completed manuscript review

observed.teacherSlideTextRead: Actual OOXML slides 34-48, with prerequisite slides 26-33 and next-topic slides 49-51 inspected for boundary context
observed.textbookTextRead: Printed 591-593 and 597; printed 592 identified as physical investigation, not new assigned activity
observed.nativeBoundaryRead: Four teaching blocks, exact note sections, header instructions and required-task demands

sequence.priorUnderstanding: A gamete contributes one allele per locus; appearance can hide a recessive allele; offspring evidence constrains parental genotypes.
sequence.teacherIntroduction: Mendel had followed one characteristic at a time. Explain why following height and pod colour together lets us ask whether inheriting one form favours another.
sequence.visual: Actual slide35image32: tall/short plants and green/yellow pods, before the generation-result diagrams.
sequence.notice: Compare height separately from pod colour, then identify the four possible phenotype combinations.
sequence.explanation: Two characteristics require tracking two allele pairs, while one gamete still contributes one allele at each studied locus.
sequence.independentReadiness: Distinguish a parent's two-locus genotype from a gamete's one-allele-per-locus label.

sequence.job: Establish and follow the experimental generations
sequence.priorUnderstanding: True-breeding history, controlled parentage, P/F1/F2 and complete dominance.
sequence.teacherIntroduction: Introduce the actual tall/green and short/yellow starting plants, defining T/t and G/g before reading the symbols.
sequence.visual: Slides36-37 parental contrast, genotype banner and F1 contributions; slide39 F2 grid appears only after its question is introduced.
sequence.notice: Read each generation in order. All F1 plants have both dominant appearances; F2 includes combinations absent from P.
sequence.explanation: The F2 observations raise a question about how the two loci travel into gametes. Do not announce the whole solution in the first paragraph.
sequence.independentReadiness: Trace how the known P contributions create TtGg F1 plants; describe the F2 phenotype groups before explaining their probabilities.

sequence.job: Explain the chromosome basis of independent assortment
sequence.priorUnderstanding: Homologues separate in meiosis I, sisters in meiosis II; allele versions differ from physical copied loci.
sequence.teacherIntroduction: Return to the two-locus question and connect independent orientations of different chromosome pairs to allele combinations.
sequence.visual: Slide41image44, guided comparison of long and short chromosome pairs across its two orientations; optional original native branch diagram afterwards.
sequence.notice: One pair's orientation can stay the same while the other reverses. Bottom endpoints represent allele contributions across different meioses.
sequence.explanation: Assortment within a parent justifies the four equally likely gamete types under the stated model; fertilisation is a separate event. In plants, the haploid products precede the stages that produce gametes.
sequence.independentReadiness: Derive TG/Tg/tG/tg and their probabilities instead of memorizing a four-letter list.

sequence.job: Connect gametes to offspring and phenotype probabilities
sequence.priorUnderstanding: Weighted gametes, independent parental contributions, separate genotype-to-phenotype rules.
sequence.teacherIntroduction: Explain why each edge of the F2 grid contains a gamete and each interior entry contains an offspring genotype.
sequence.visual: Slide39image40 and readable native tables, with explicit circle/square and green/yellow legend meanings.
sequence.notice: Locate TtGg in repeated pairings; count cells, then regroup by phenotype. Each underscore belongs to its own locus.
sequence.explanation: Separate 16 contribution pairs from distinct genotype classes; derive 9:3:3:1 under this cross's assumptions. Explain multiplication of independent requirements and addition of mutually exclusive alternatives.
sequence.independentReadiness: Diagnose a plausible-looking incomplete gamete list and distinguish homozygosity at both loci from two dominant phenotypes, without pre-answering the exact required tasks.

sequence.job: Transfer the method to the original tomato cross
sequence.priorUnderstanding: The grid follows distinct weighted gametes, not a fixed 4-by-4 template.
sequence.teacherIntroduction: Explicitly switch from pea pod colour/height to tomato fruit colour/height and redefine R/r and T/t.
sequence.visual: Teacher slides43-45 method and native readable 4-by-2 tables; source image43 is only a small allele-combination aid, not a full worked solution.
sequence.notice: RrTt makes four distinct gametes; rrTt makes two. Every interior pairing has probability 1/8.
sequence.explanation: Translate worded parents, justify gamete lists, combine loci, group genotype separately from phenotype, check totals, then interpret expected proportions.
sequence.independentReadiness: Retain the COMPLETE unchanged change-parent optional task with its existing native response, hint and model.

sequence.job: Use offspring evidence before predicting the squash cross
sequence.priorUnderstanding: A dominant appearance leaves the second allele uncertain; a recessive offspring requires contributions from both parents.
sequence.teacherIntroduction: Explain why this problem begins with missing parental information rather than supplied genotypes. Switch explicitly to fruit-colour and fruit-shape W/w and D/d rules.
sequence.visual: Slides46-47 worded source problem and native allele/evidence tables; no invented squash image required to replace a clear reasoning table.
sequence.notice: wwD_ and W_dd each contain a genuine unknown. The observed wwdd offspring supplies evidence at both loci.
sequence.explanation: Resolve the parents before deriving two gametes each, a 2-by-2 grid, and expectations among 80 scored offspring plants. Separate the inference from the subsequent prediction.
sequence.independentReadiness: Retain the COMPLETE unchanged flower/leaf evidence task where only one parental blank is forced; explain the limit of smooth-only observations.

sequence.job: Answer the initial question and set the next boundary
sequence.priorUnderstanding: The method remains genotype, gametes, contributions, phenotype interpretation under stated assumptions.
sequence.teacherIntroduction: Conclude when one allele contribution does not favour another and why two traits alone do not guarantee 9:3:3:1.
sequence.notice: Compare pea, tomato and squash grids and the information each problem supplied.
sequence.explanation: Briefly name linked loci as a later boundary and naturally introduce changed dominance relationships next, without internal route-code narration.
sequence.independentReadiness: Attempt the unchanged supported and required tasks using explained methods; optional later-dominance textbook questions remain deferred.

visualCautions: Slide37 repeats identical TG and tg labels in a 4-by-4 display. Explain that each homozygous parent has one distinct gamete type; do not teach 16 distinct outcomes from this redundant grid.
Slide39image40 is static and already displays the 9:3:3:1 result. Guide reading honestly; do not promise a scripted staged reveal.

Slide41image47 includes recombinant colour segments. Colour is parental-origin context rather than a claim that every sister chromatid remains identical after crossing over. Prefer the simpler image44 for the main orientation account.
Slide41 wording names meiosis II while describing metaphase I. The learner explanation must distinguish them correctly.
Slide47 fruit-versus-flower source typo and printed593 overbroad ratio/underscore caption are corrected only in explanatory copy, never by editing frozen sources.
Native diagram bottom A/B/C/D location labels are not four additional allele symbols; keep approved labeling mappings intact.
